chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Ali ibn Ri'ab, on the authority of Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon him) that he used to say:

Animals recognize four things: their recognition of their Lord, the Blessed and Exalted; their recognition of death; their recognition of the female from the male; and their recognition of the lush pasture.
ai.seo_question: What four things do animals recognize according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Hussein (Zayn al-Abidin) highlights the innate divine wisdom (*fitrah*) embedded in animal nature, distinguishing their instinctual recognition from human intellectual knowledge. This narration underscores the Shia theological view that creation possesses an inherent, God-given awareness of its origins, mortality, and sustenance, serving as a sign (*ayah*) of the Creator's meticulous design.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-136 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Ali ibn Re’ab, on the authority of Abi Hamzih that Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB) said, “
Animals can recognize four things: their Lord - the Blessed the Sublime; death; male and female; and pastures.”
